extracted.intended_audience: Berkeley Math Circle participants, instructors, and parents (K–12 students and their teachers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and recommendations for which textbooks and problem-solving books are appropriate for Berkeley Math Circle participants at various K–12 levels, and for instructors/parents running math circles. Includes per-book descriptions, target levels, and curricular goals for grade-specific textbooks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability policy for BMC book sales
rubrics_metrics.description: The Berkeley Math Circle and Math Taught the Right Way will be providing some of these required and recommended books to participants, teachers, and instructors at a discounted price (please note that we will not be making the books available to anyone else).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books at the BMC website are for registered students only and are not sold to people not registered at BMC; books may alternatively be purchased on the web; available for purchase at Monday or Wednesday office hours while in stock.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strongly recommended: 'A Decade of the Berkeley Math Circle' Volumes I & II
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections based on BMC sessions with a wide variety of topics, treatments of many methods of proof, emphasis on ways of thinking via ~100 problem solving techniques, and ~300 problems ranging beginner to intermediate with occasional advanced problems and open questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Book encourages applying acquired knowledge to problems, rarely gives ready answers, emphasizes learning from mistakes via discussions of non-proofs and common problem solving pitfalls; good for committing to mastering techniques by doing problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Eastern-European adapted textbooks for middle/high-school (grades 6–9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Textbooks for grades 6-9 (6A, 6B, 7A, 7B, 8A, 8B, 9A; 9B in preparation), each grade split into two semesters with a textbook and workbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These books are used at Math Taught the Right Way and are highly recommended to students at BMC if they feel that math taught at their school is not challenging enough for them.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6A curriculum core goals
rubrics_metrics.description: In 6A, a core goal is to develop basic numeracy — students study algebraic operations and their properties, encounter natural numbers and decimals, begin work with variables to set up a solid base for later books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometry focus on more complicated polyhedral and round solids; algebra includes ratios, proportions, data representation and practical problems (recipe and map scaling); semester ends with study of polynomials and familiar factoring formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8B (and preparatory later grades) curriculum goals
rubrics_metrics.description: For 8B algebra: basics of algebraic functions and their graphs; solving systems of linear equations and inequalities; polynomial equations; rational expressions. Geometry: rigorous development of classic theorems on circles and inscribed angles and polygons. Final chapter introduces combinatorics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Later work continues functions, systems of quadratic equations, methods for solving inequalities (polynomials, rational expressions, absolute value), geometry unit on similar triangles to set the stage for trigonometry (9B), and probabilistic results developed from combinatorics learned in 8B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art and Craft of Problem Solving — problem-solving pedagogy
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduces a problem-solving approach to mathematics rather than traditional exercises; aims to develop strong problem solving skills by encouraging students to do math.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals to everyone from college-level majors to independent learners; author draws on IMO coaching experience to give an enhanced sense of mathematics and ability to investigate and solve problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kiselev's Geometry (Book I Planimetry) — plane geometry foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: A wonderful, easy-going introduction to plane geometry; historically used as a regular textbook in Russian middle schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translated into English and suitable as a solid, classical introduction to plane geometry for middle-school level instruction or self-study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kiselev's Geometry (Book II Stereometry) — stereometry foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: A self-contained exposition on stereometry, a continuation of Kiselev's classical geometry work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proven favorite across generations; suitable for building solid 3D geometry understanding following plane geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math Circle by the Bay (Grades 1–5) — elementary math-circle guide
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on topics taught in elementary math circles; intended for people running math circles or parents, and bright fourth or fifth graders may read it on their own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main features: logical sequence of problems, descriptions of class reactions, hints for kids when stuck; balances inspiring original approaches with enough detail for a fallback lesson if teacher needs a prepared lesson on short notice; introduces combinatorics, Fibonacci numbers, Pascal's triangle, notion of area, and topics with deep mathematical context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Circles: Russian Experience — extracurricular-math approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Book predicated on the Russian mathematical circles tradition; intended for students and teachers who love mathematics and want to study beyond school curriculum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as both mathematical recreation and substantial theoretical/problem material in extracurricular mathematics; useful for organizing study groups and deepening beyond-school mathematics exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math Olympiad Contest Problems (Elementary & Middle) — contest practice for younger students
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections of challenging contest problems aimed at young students, with a variety of problems, hints to help readers get started, and appendices that inform and enrich.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for students, teachers and parents preparing for contests; provides exposure to many problem styles and starter hints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art of Problem Solving (AoPS) texts — for outstanding middle/high-school students
rubrics_metrics.description: Curriculum specifically designed for outstanding math students in grades 6-12; presents broader and deeper exploration than typical curricula and is used by many winners of major national contests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended for high-performing students preparing for competitions (MATHCOUNTS, AMC, etc.) and for those seeking deeper problem-solving curriculum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs That Really Count — combinatorial proof techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrates many number patterns via counting arguments and correspondences; explores more than 200 identities and emphasizes combinatorial proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes numerous hints and references, appeals to readers from high school students to professional mathematicians; suitable for learning combinatorial proof methods and identities in need of combinatorial proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Count Down — narrative about IMO contestants (inspiration/context)
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative following six IMO contestants, exploring what drives contestants and contextual questions about math culture and talent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended for advanced students interested in contest culture and inspiration; provides background and motivation rather than direct instructional content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contest Problem Books (AMC 10 & AMC 12 collections) — past-contest practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections of past AMC 10 and AMC 12 tests with complete solutions, useful for students preparing for these contests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides realistic practice on past contests (e.g., AMC 10 tests 2000–2007, AMC 12 tests 2001–2007); recommended for students targeting contest readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Omnibus — broad enrichment lectures
rubrics_metrics.description: Thirty lectures on diverse classical mathematics topics covering material outside standard undergraduate/graduate curriculum; contains exercises, selected solutions, many drawings and portraits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good for readers seeking breadth and connections across algebra, combinatorics, geometry, and topology; most lectures contain surprises even for seasoned researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical Adventures For Students and Amateurs — assorted lecture topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Collection of lectures aimed primarily at bright high school students (and their teachers, parents, and interested adults) addressing a wide variety of entertaining and serious mathematical questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suitable for high-school-level enrichment and exposing students to diverse mathematical problems and ideas beyond standard curricula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation-level labels for choosing books (Suggested/Recommended/Highly Recommended/Strongly Recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Books on the page are explicitly labeled with recommendation levels (e.g., 'Strongly Recommended Books', 'Highly Recommended for BMC Beginner and Intermediate', 'Suggested for BMC Elementary and Beginner', 'Recommended for BMC Beginner, Intermediate and Advanced', 'Recommended for BMC Advanced').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these labels to match book difficulty and purpose to participant level: 'Suggested' → elementary/beginner; 'Highly Recommended' → beginner/intermediate; 'Recommended' → range including advanced; 'Strongly Recommended' → flagship BMC collections.
